text:
sam-runtime: Heads up — hitting unexpectedly high GPU memory when running 8-way tensor-parallel inference on the 70B model. Peak per-GPU ~= 14.2GB vs expected ~11GB. Not a model weight issue; looks like transient comm / temp buffers

sam-runtime: Attached a quick nvprof/pyprof snapshot — big chunks labelled as comm buffers and aten::empty temp tensors during TP reduce/concat. Also we see a few large cudaMallocs around attention kernel launches.

sam-runtime: Repro on staging with batch-size 1, seq 2048, streaming off. Single-GPU runs fine. Multi-GPU scales up more than linearly. Thoughts? :eyes:

profiling-bot: Profiling summary (short):
- total device mem used: 14.2 GB
- model weights: 8.9 GB
- KV cache: 1.2 GB
- comm buffers (nccl/custom): 1.9 GB
- temporaries/allocator rounding: 1.2 GB
- free/fragmentation: 0.0 GB

anya-ml: Thanks for the dump. Two quick hypotheses: 1) our comm wrapper preallocates per-stream comm buffers and they're not reused across TP shards, 2) allocator workspace/threshold causing many small allocations to round up.

devin-engineer: Can you paste the short pprof stack for the big mallocs? we might be doing cudaMalloc for workspace per attention call instead of using a pooled buffer.

sam-runtime: Pasted snippet:
```
malloc_large 1.0GB  -> attention_forward  -> fused_attention_kernel -> cudaLaunchKernel
nccl_alloc  1.9GB  -> all_reduce_async -> comm_send_recv -> cudaMemcpyAsync
aten::empty  512MB -> transpose -> concat -> reduce_scatter
```

sam-runtime: The nccl_alloc label is our internal comm buffer malloc (we wrap nccl calls to allocate staging buffers for reduce_scatter).

leo-infra: That staging buffer size seems suspiciously close to the per-chunk slice size. Are we allocating per-TensorParallel slice and not reusing?

anya-ml: Exactly. For TP we slice batch across 8 devices; if we allocate a staging buffer sized for the full slice each op that'll multiply. We should be able to reuse one buffer per op-stream or use a single preallocated pool per GPU sized to max concurrent comms.

devin-engineer: Another lever: our attention kernels request a workspace size computed pessimistically (max_seq * head_dim * 2) and then we call cudaMalloc every forward. Replace with a long-lived workspace buffer and only cudaMalloc if needed at grow time. That would avoid repeated fragmentation and rounding.

sam-runtime: Agree. I also noticed allocator reports many small free segments being left behind after large frees. We use a simple caching allocator with 256KB bin granularity. Might need a new growth strategy and coalescing pass.

anya-ml: Quick experiment suggestion: instrument the comm wrapper to reuse a per-GPU nccl staging buffer and run the same script. I can put a patch that returns the buffer to a pool instead of freeing. Should reduce the ~1.9GB -> ~128MB if we reuse.

devin-engineer: I'll prototype a persistent workspace pool for attention kernels. We'll expose a config: --workspace-max-per-gpu and a growth threshold. Start at 2GB and see if it prevents repeated cudaMalloc churn.

leo-infra: Also check NCCL parameters. If we do many small all-reduces, NCCL may internally allocate rings. There's an env var we can tune for proto/collective buffer sizing; but first try to eliminate our extra staging buffers.

sam-runtime: Running quick patch now to reuse one staging buffer per-GPU/stream. Will report back in ~15m.

profiling-bot: New run (w/ reuse staging buffer):
- total device mem used: 11.6 GB
- model weights: 8.9 GB
- KV cache: 1.2 GB
- comm buffers (reused): 0.14 GB
- temporaries: 0.9 GB
- fragmentation: 0.0 GB

sam-runtime: Nice — peak dropped to ~11.6GB. So most of the extra was our staging allocation multiplicity.

anya-ml: Good win. Next: address the temporary allocations and allocator rounding. If we maintain a long-lived pooled workspace for attention and reduce-scatter, temporaries should shrink too.

devin-engineer: I have a small patch ready to switch allocator bins to 64KB granularity and add an active pool for "attention_workspace" with LRU eviction. Will run perf after.

leo-infra: One caveat — pinned memory vs device memory allocation behavior can change latency. Make sure we don't increase CPU-to-GPU latency by over-pinning. Keep option flags for pinned vs device pool.

sam-runtime: Action items we agreed: 
- (anya) land staging-buffer reuse in comm wrapper (hotfix)
- (devin) implement persistent attention workspace pool + reduce cudaMallocs
- (leo) audit NCCL env flags and doc recommended settings for TP inference
- (sam) add a microbench harness to reproduce memory footprint across seq lengths and TP widths and add to CI perf job

devin-engineer: I'll open PRs for the allocator and workspace. Will include a small benchmark: 1/2/4/8 TP runs, seq 512/1024/2048.

anya-ml: After PRs I'll run extended runs on 8xA100 to validate memory headroom and check no perf regressions.

sam-runtime: Thanks all. If anyone spots other unexpected cudaMallocs in the profile ping me; I left the raw traces in /mnt/staging/profiles/1768459021/ . :thumbsup:

leo-infra: Great writeup. Let's make sure to capture the cost savings in follow-up release note (reduced mem footprint for TP inference).

profiling-bot: Thread closed (profiling snapshot archived).
